assessments.reasoning: The fresh HTTPS retrieval from https://polyformproject.org/licenses/perimeter/1.0.1.txt returned HTTP 200. The title and embedded edition link both identify 1.0.1. The acquisition reports SHA-256 0687d1249bde50ecb2db5b8e32f3a6d9cb24a7acfeaa346341654ca47a5302ac for bytes [1714,2321), matching the supplied locator. The cited clauses directly support both parts of the conditional claim, and the definitions confirm which software and actor they address.

limitations: The assessment assumes the work is offered under this edition and the actor relies on its permissions for the conduct.
When the actor markets a substitute without using the covered software, the marketing sentence leaves the product’s competitive status open.
Classifying a particular product requires facts about that product. Enforceability and statutory rights require separate legal evidence. The edition expressly preserves fair use rights.
reasoning: PolyForm Perimeter License 1.0.1 expressly excludes “providing to others any product that competes with the software” from permitted purposes. The Competition section supplies a sufficient condition for classifying a product as competing. The actor must “use this software to market a product as a substitute for the functionality or value of the software” for that sentence to apply. The definitions tie “software” to the work the licensor offers under these terms and “use” to conduct requiring one of the actor’s licenses.
